task_completion.description: The medical image (CT scan) is successfully loaded into the viewer interface.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A DICOM/CT image is visible in the main viewport of the application.

task_completion.description: The agent selects the arrow annotation tool from the toolbar.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The arrow icon in the toolbar is highlighted, or the cursor changes to a crosshair/drawing mode.

task_completion.description: An arrow annotation is drawn onto the medical image.
task_completion.visual_evidence: An arrow graphic is visible overlaid on the CT image slices.

task_completion.description: The annotation color is changed to red.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The arrow annotation on the image appears red (R > 150, G < 80, B < 80).

task_completion.description: The line thickness of the annotation is set to at least 3.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The properties panel or line settings show a value of 3 or higher, and the arrow appears visibly thicker than the default line.

task_completion.description: The view is exported as a PNG to the specific directory and filename requested.
task_completion.visual_evidence: An export dialog or file explorer shows the path ~/DICOM/exports/publication_figure.png being typed or saved.

integrity.description: The agent used the application GUI to create the annotation rather than script injection.
integrity.visual_evidence: Screenshots show the mouse cursor interacting with the drawing tools and property panels.

integrity.description: The agent used the software's export/save function.
integrity.visual_evidence: The 'Export' or 'Save As' menu/dialog is visible in the trajectory.

integrity.description: The agent did not use the terminal to move or rename a pre-existing image to the target path.
integrity.visual_evidence: The terminal is not used to execute 'mv' or 'cp' commands for the final output file.

privileged_info_for_vlm: The target file must be a PNG located at /home/ga/DICOM/exports/publication_figure.png. The annotation must be Red (specifically high Red channel values compared to Green/Blue) and have a thickness setting of 3 or greater. The patient data in the image should correspond to PatientID: ANN001.
